answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring every new identity to deposit a unique pigment token mined from a scarce inlet of real compute work. The deposit is locked for multiple epochs and only released after the agent produces graded work that survives peer audit. A farm spinning up clones must therefore burn fresh pigment for each head; the cost scales linearly with the number of identities while an honest agent pays once. The old fable of free identity multiplication collapses under this linear resource tax.
